findings.summary: Candidate 6 did not update the brief's by-index list of changed v5 data or its question-2 counts. Line 98 says 'Everything else, `types` included, is v5's', but v5 type rows 33-36 now differ from v5. Line 94 says 74 assertions are appended (132-205); it is now 82 (132-213). Line 107 gives 206 assertions, 4,519 access checks and 106 mutation checks; it is now 214, 4,600 and 114. Line 33 says vectors.json 'appends' the new checks. In fact they are inserted inside each kind group (Q98-Q109 after Q97, N41-N49 after N40, M107-M109 and M110-M114 inside their mutation groups), so candidate 5's v6-only vectors move: access checks from index 4439, mutation checks from index 94.
findings.evidence: Comparing matrix.json types with ../selinux-matrix-v3/matrix.json by index, only 33-36 differ, each by the appended narrowed init_t entries. IDs and expectations of every candidate-5 vector are unchanged, and v5 positions (access 0-2434, mutation 0-75) are kept, as README:58 claims. README:49, :59-60 and :75-76 state the change correctly. Earlier inaccuracies confined to the brief while the README was correct (XR4-2, XV5-2) were NOTEs.
findings.requiredChange: Update REVIEW_BRIEF.md lines 33, 94, 98 and 107 to candidate 6's data (types 33-36; 82 appended assertions, 132-213; 214/4,600/114; 'inserted within each kind group').

findings.summary: check_matrix's named-type-transition rule tests 'the source may write the parent' with granted(), which ignores a classes/perms narrowing. v5 never narrowed WRITE, so the test was exact. Under candidate 6, init_t's narrowed `sock_file unlink` counts as WRITE, so check_matrix now accepts a named type transition from init_t under a planeon socket-file parent, which candidate 5 refused. The delta therefore changes check_matrix behaviour outside _cleanup_grant, although the brief says the evaluator adds 'nothing else'.
findings.evidence: Scratch mutation: append typeTransitions {source: init_t, parent: planeon_i05_sock_t, class: sock_file, name: x.sock, new: planeon_i05_sock_t}. Candidate 5 refuses it ('type transition ...'). Candidate 6 accepts it, and all 214 assertions hold. The rule can never fire, because Linux v6.12 selinux_determine_inode_label computes a new inode's type from its parent directory and a socket inode has no children. No allowed() answer changes, so the effect is inert.
findings.requiredChange: Optional: test the parent with _granted_file(..., 'dir', 'add_name'), or require 'dir' in the parent type's classes, and add a mutation. Otherwise disclose the side effect.

findings.summary: _cleanup_grant maps each socket-file type to one listener through a dict built over `sockets`. If two socket rows name the same file type, only the last row's listener counts, and check_matrix does not require one socket row per socket-file type.
findings.evidence: Two-op scratch mutation: append a socket row {object: planeon_x_socket_t, listener: planeon_gate_t, file: qualk8s_runtime_sock_t, connect: []}, plus the narrowed init_t unlink on qualk8s_runtime_sock_t. check_matrix accepts it and all 214 assertions hold, and allowed(init_t, qualk8s_runtime_sock_t, sock_file, unlink) becomes True. Only access check N45 would flip; no assertion pins the backend socket files against init_t. The reverse (a backend-listener row appended for planeon_i05_sock_t) fails closed. As with XV5-1, the route needs a visible change to another row, so this is defence in depth, not an open route.
findings.requiredChange: Optional: in check_matrix, require every socket row that names the type to have a resident listener (or one row per socket-file type). Optionally also add an assertion that init_t neither stats nor unlinks qualk8s_datastore_sock_t or qualk8s_runtime_sock_t.

findings.summary: A79.<type> lists the READ, WRITE and RELABEL permissions other than getattr and unlink. Its statement ('systemd may only stat and unlink', matrix.json:7137 and siblings) and the README Assertions row ('may do nothing else to it') claim more than that. An EXECUTE, EXECUTE_NO_TRANS or EXECMOD grant to init_t on a planeon socket-file type passes check_matrix and every assertion.
findings.evidence: Scratch mutation setting access.EXECUTE = [{domain: init_t}] on planeon_i05_sock_t: check_matrix passes and failed_assertions is empty. check_matrix refuses ENTRYPOINT (the XV4-1 rule). The gap is inert in Linux v6.12: may_open returns -EACCES for MAY_EXEC on an S_IFSOCK inode before inode_permission, so no exec reaches the SELinux execute check. README:79-80 already states the true scope ('no other READ, WRITE or RELABEL permission').
findings.requiredChange: Optional: narrow A79's statement and the README row to 'no other READ, WRITE or RELABEL permission', or add the remaining file-class permissions to A79.

findings.summary: The removal works under the pinned matrix, and the matrix closes no permission it needs. Two premises are worth stating. (a) Q106-Q109 pin only dir search, write, remove_name and rmdir. The cleanup also opens, lists and stats the directory (dir open, read, getattr); init_t's unconditional v5 READ on planeon_run_t grants these, but no check pins them. (b) The directory type. systemd creates RuntimeDirectory= paths with its label-aware mkdir, which sets an fscreate context from the loaded file contexts, and selinux_determine_inode_label prefers that fscreate SID over a named type transition or inheritance. So /run/planeon, live-proxy and maintenance carry planeon_run_t only if W03's file contexts say so, while README:661-668 names only the named type transition for systemd's /run/planeon. By my reading, a base-policy /run/.* entry would otherwise give var_run_t, and host policy would then decide the cleanup.
findings.evidence: Kernel facts (Linux v6.12, security/selinux/hooks.c and fs/namei.c), from my own knowledge. unlink: may_delete -> inode_permission(dir, MAY_WRITE|MAY_EXEC) -> selinux_inode_permission gives dir write+search; selinux_inode_unlink -> may_link(MAY_UNLINK) gives dir search+remove_name on the directory, then sock_file unlink on the victim (its inode class). rmdir: the same on the parent, plus dir rmdir via may_link(MAY_RMDIR). Path walk: may_lookup -> dir search. stat: selinux_inode_getattr -> getattr. Opening and listing: selinux_inode_permission(MAY_READ) and selinux_file_open (dir read, open), then selinux_file_permission from iterate_dir (dir read). connect: unix_find_bsd -> path_permission(MAY_WRITE) -> sock_file write, which A79 denies to init_t. systemd facts, also my own knowledge: on stop the manager (PID 1, init_t) removes each RuntimeDirectory= leaf (planeon/live-proxy, planeon/maintenance; not /run/planeon) via exec_context_destroy_runtime_directory -> rm_rf(path, REMOVE_ROOT). Some versions fstatat each non-directory entry (hence sock_file getattr). rm_rf's temporary-filesystem test (statfs -> selinux_sb_statfs -> filesystem getattr on /run's tmpfs superblock) has a host label outside the matrix. Scratch check: allowed(init_t, planeon_run_t, dir, p) is True for open, read, getattr, search, write, remove_name and rmdir in all three states, and var_run_t answers None. The grant cannot tell a stale socket from a live one, and I01, I02 and I05 share live-proxy. README:90-92 rightly assigns that, and the shared-RuntimeDirectory semantics, to HS53/W03/T04.
findings.requiredChange: Optional: add access checks for init_t dir open, read and getattr on planeon_run_t. Also record a W03/T04 obligation that the file contexts label /run/planeon and its RuntimeDirectory= leaves planeon_run_t, because systemd's label-aware mkdir overrides the named type transition.
